# Logic Apps Standard — Troubleshooting Dashboard

Import this workbook, select your **Subscription**, **App Service Plan (WS-1/WS-2/WS-3)**, **Logic App / Function App**, backing **Storage Account**, (optionally) **Cosmos DB account**, and (optionally) a **Log Analytics Workspace** below. All panels are scoped to your selections.

**What this answers:**
- Which workflow runs are failing, and what's the error? (requires Log Analytics — see Section 1)
- Is the App Service Plan CPU/Memory genuinely pegged, and when did it start?
- Is a trigger or workflow looping/retrying even though nothing shows as "active"?
- Is the backing storage account throttling (429s), causing the host to spin?
- Is Cosmos DB RU-throttling causing retry storms?

**On historical data:** the metrics in Sections 1-4 (CPU%, Queue Length, Function executions, Storage/Cosmos metrics) are **platform metrics Azure collects automatically for every resource, retained 93 days** — this works retroactively, even for dates before this workbook was imported. Default time range below is set to 14 days; widen it up to 90 days using the picker to see the full pre-deployment history.

**What does NOT retroactively exist:** detailed diagnostic/trigger-level logs and Application Insights telemetry only start flowing from the moment Diagnostic Settings / App Insights are enabled on the resource — if that wasn't already on, there's no historical detail at that granularity, only the coarse metrics above.

> Tip: Pin this workbook to a dashboard and set auto-refresh to 5 min during the pre-go-live window.

parameters.name: AppServicePlan
parameters.label: App Service Plan (WS-1/WS-2/WS-3)
parameters.query:
Resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.web/serverfarms'
| where subscriptionId == '{Subscription:id}'
| project value = id, label = name
| order by label asc

parameters.name: LogicApp
parameters.label: Logic App / Function App (Standard)
parameters.query:
Resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.web/sites'
| where subscriptionId == '{Subscription:id}'
| where kind has 'workflowapp' or kind has 'functionapp'
| project value = id, label = name
| order by label asc

parameters.name: StorageAccount
parameters.label: Backing Storage Account
parameters.query:
Resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.storage/storageaccounts'
| where subscriptionId == '{Subscription:id}'
| project value = id, label = name
| order by label asc

parameters.name: CosmosAccount
parameters.label: Cosmos DB Account (optional)
parameters.query:
Resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.documentdb/databaseaccounts'
| where subscriptionId == '{Subscription:id}'
| project value = id, label = name
| order by label asc

parameters.name: LogAnalyticsWorkspace
parameters.label: Log Analytics Workspace (optional — needed for Section 1)
parameters.query:
Resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.operationalinsights/workspaces'
| where subscriptionId == '{Subscription:id}'
| project value = id, label = name
| order by label asc

content.json:
## 1. Workflow Run History & Errors
**Requires:** Diagnostic Settings on the Logic App sending `WorkflowRuntime` logs to the **Log Analytics Workspace** selected above. If this section returns nothing, either diagnostics aren't flowing yet (see Section 6) or your workspace uses a different table/column schema than assumed below.

**This is a starting query, not a guaranteed-exact one** — exact column names vary depending on whether your Diagnostic Settings export as "Azure diagnostics" (classic, table `AzureDiagnostics`) or "resource-specific" (dedicated table, commonly `LogicAppWorkflowRuntime`). The query below searches both so it works either way; if it returns rows, inspect the raw columns in the **Logs** blade to refine filters further.

content.query:
search in (AzureDiagnostics, LogicAppWorkflowRuntime) _ResourceId =~ "{LogicApp}"
| where Level in ("Error", "Warning") or tostring(column_ifexists("status_s", "")) in ("Failed", "TimedOut", "Aborted")
| project TimeGenerated, Level, Type, Message = coalesce(column_ifexists("Message", ""), column_ifexists("properties_message_s", "")), Status = column_ifexists("status_s", "")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
| take 200
content.title: Failed / errored / warning log entries (last 200)

content.query:
search in (AzureDiagnostics, LogicAppWorkflowRuntime) _ResourceId =~ "{LogicApp}"
| where Level in ("Error", "Warning") or tostring(column_ifexists("status_s", "")) in ("Failed", "TimedOut", "Aborted")
| summarize Count = count() by bin(TimeGenerated, 15m), Level
| order by TimeGenerated asc
content.title: Error/warning volume over time — spikes here should correlate with CPU spikes in Section 2

content.json:
## 2. App Service Plan — CPU & Memory
Sustained >80-85% for 10+ min on a plan with no active workflows is the key red flag.

content.title: App Service Plan: CPU % and Memory % (Avg)
Http Queue Length — climbing with no active traffic = host-level stall

content.json:
## 3. Logic App / Function host — execution & duration
A trigger firing far more often than expected (recurrence misconfigured, polling trigger stuck) shows up here even if the workflow displays as "disabled".

## 4. Backing Storage Account — throttling check
Logic Apps Standard relies on `WEBSITE_CONTENTAZUREFILECONNECTIONSTRING`. Storage throttling (429s) or high latency here causes the Functions host to spin and retry — this shows up as CPU with no visible workflow run.

content.title: Storage Transactions (filter by ResponseType = ClientThrottlingError in Azure Monitor metric split for 429s)

content.json:
## 5. Cosmos DB backend — RU throttling (if applicable)
If a query or change feed is hitting RU limits, Logic Apps retries aggressively — burning CPU with no obvious "workflow run" to point at.

content.title: Total Request Units Consumed (split by StatusCode in metric blade to isolate 429s)

content.json:
## 6. Recommended alert rules (set these up once, not just view)

| Alert | Scope | Condition | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| High sustained CPU | App Service Plan | CPU Percentage (Avg) > 85% for 10 min | Catches the exact "steady near-100%" pattern reported |
| Queue buildup | App Service Plan | Http Queue Length > 0 sustained | Confirms host-level stall vs. real traffic |
| Storage throttling | Storage Account | Transactions (429 split) > 0 | Root-cause signal, not visible elsewhere |
| Cosmos RU throttling | Cosmos DB | Normalized RU Consumption > 90% | Root-cause signal for retry storms |
| Function error spike | Logic App / Function App | Http5xx > 5 in 5 min | Confirms trigger/dependency failures |
| Workflow run failures | Log Analytics (scheduled query rule, not a metric alert) | Count of Failed/TimedOut runs > 0 in 15 min | Direct signal from Section 1 — catches failures even when CPU/metrics look normal |

**⚠️ Action needed now, not after go-live:** if **Diagnostic Settings** are not already enabled on the Logic App resource, detailed trigger-level logs and exception traces (including everything Section 1 depends on) are **not being captured at all** — there is no historical backfill once you turn this on. Every day this stays off is a day of log detail you'll never get back if the issue recurs.

**Enable it today:** Logic App resource → **Diagnostic settings** → **Add diagnostic setting** → check **AllMetrics** + **WorkflowRuntime** (or **FunctionAppLogs**) → destination **Send to Log Analytics workspace**. Takes under 5 minutes and starts the clock immediately — with limited time to go-live, every day of logs collected now is a day you won't have to reconstruct from coarse metrics alone later.
